text.p: Italian debt markets ended around 60 basis points down after supports caved in in a generally edgy market, despite a relatively steady lira.
"The sell off began at the short end of the curve and then the BTP came down, without any apparent reason," one broker in London said.

The global focus is on Tuesday's FOMC meeting with investors waiting to see whether the Fed raises U.S. interest rates and if so by how much. But on the domestic front, brokers noted a report by JP Morgan which forecast Italian CPI falling below two percent in April, opening the way to an interest rate cut.
The November 2006 Btp ended 61 basis points down at 100.28 yielding 7.84 percent and with a spread over Germany of 194 bps. The most traded July 2006 Btp was 81 basis points off at 105.18.

The July Btp future on LIFFE was wallowing 55 basis points down at 124.53 after breaking support at 125.00, which opened the way to stop loss sales. Brokers said short covering had hauled it back off the day's lows and they expected it to remain here for the short term.
At home the focus is on the government's mini-budget due to be announced towards the end of the week, with the package to include 15-16 trillion lire of budget deficit slashing measures.
"But we don't expect anything structural because they haven't got the force to do that," a broker said.

The markets have wanted Prime Minister Romano Prodi to address spending in the welfare state, particularly state pensions. But few expect such steps will be included in the package because of the lack of support for them in parliament among key Prodi allies the Communist Refoundation party.
